Home

Killzone HD: Unofficial PC Port (static recompilation)

A native Linux and Windows x64 port of the 2011 PS3 remaster of the first Killzone, made by static recompilation: the game's PowerPC and SPU code is translated to C++ ahead of time and compiled into a PC program on your machine; graphics go through Vulkan. No emulator runs at play time.

Status: Playable

You need your own copy of the game. This project ships no game code, data, assets or keys.

InstallSee the statusSource on GitHub

Unreleased

not released yet

  • ChangedF12 no longer takes a developer capture (a capture_<date>_<time> folder in the game's folder): it was on in every build, and F12 is also Steam's screenshot key. Developers turn it on with PS3RECOMP_CAPTURE_KEY=1 (ps3recomp patch 2089).

0.7.0

23 Nov 2026 · pre-release

  • AddedReporting a crash (#129): when the game closes unexpectedly (a crash, a hang, a lost GPU, killed, an error code; not when you quit), the launcher says what the exit code means and shows the crash signature, and offers to make the support package; after it, to open the bug report form on GitHub with the version, system and signature filled in (only on a yes; the zip is never uploaded). A session that never ended (power loss) is named at the next start. work/play.log now ends with [launcher] session ended: exit <code> (<meaning>) after <N> s, <kind>, and work/logs/sessions.jsonl keeps one line per session.
  • AddedThe support package also holds the earlier game logs, sessions.jsonl, the game's crash and hang reports with the names of its functions (from your own build's symbol table), Windows' error reports for the game and its display driver events of the last 24 hours (on Linux the kernel log's GPU lines), what the game's log says about the PC, and a line of your own when you make it in a terminal. scripts/support.cmd and scripts/support.sh make it in the Windows zip and the Linux folder, as the setup's Start menu entry does; RecompLauncher gets a "Crash reports" folder button.
  • AddedWhen the game crashes, its log now says where: a [kz-crash] block with the exception, the faulting module and offset, the thread, the uptime, the registers, up to 32 frames and a signature (KZ-XXXX-XXXX) that is the same each time the same crash happens, and a copy in work/crash/crash-*.txt. Before, a crash like the ones a few seconds into Level 1 on AMD GPUs (#129) left nothing in the log (docs/dev/crash-reports.md).
  • AddedWhen the game stops showing new frames for 5 s (and again at 30 s) while its window is not minimized, the log gets a [kz-hang] block with every thread's stack, and a copy in work/crash/hang-*.txt; the game is left running. KZ_HANG_WATCH=0 turns this off.
  • AddedThe log starts with the system it runs on: [kz-sys] lines for the system, CPU, cores, memory, monitors, the settings in kz1hd_pc.ini, the KZ_* and PS3* variables set (your home folder written as ~), what started the game and whether the build has DLSS.
  • AddedKZ_CRASH_TEST=<kind> makes the game crash or hang on purpose, to check the reports on a build.
  • AddedThe game straight from the Killzone Trilogy disc, with no RPCS3 installed: --disc FOLDER (the copied disc, or its PS3_EXTRA package) on Project Vekta.exe, ./project-vekta and the prepare scripts downloads the official RPCS3 at a pinned version (checked by SHA-256), which installs the package into the port's work folder with no window and decrypts a copy of the EBOOT there; the disc is only read and an RPCS3 of yours is not touched (docs/INSTALL.md). The setup's "Your game" page offers it as "From my Killzone Trilogy disc", and recomplauncher.json as a disc field beside the game folder. On Windows 10, 7-Zip unpacks the RPCS3 download. The PlayStation Store package still goes through "Use my RPCS3 install".
  • AddedEach release file comes with a build provenance attestation: a statement, signed through Sigstore and kept by GitHub, that the repository's release workflow built that very file from the tagged commit. gh attestation verify <file> --repo gustavomorinaga/project-vekta checks a download against it (docs/INSTALL.md).
  • AddedWhen the graphics driver stops responding (the GPU is lost), the game now says so in play.log ([RSX vulkan] device lost in ..., with the last passes the GPU was given) and ends with its own exit code, 78, whose text tells you to update the driver and report it; before, it closed without a word. A GPU that takes longer than 2 s logs GPU has not finished for N s each second. KZ_CRASH_TEST=gpu-lost tries this on a working GPU (ps3recomp patches 2084, 2085).
  • Addedplay.log names the graphics card's driver and its version (for AMD and Intel also the release, such as 24.10.1) and the card's video memory, for bug reports (patch 2082).
  • ChangedThe game logs of the last sessions are kept: each earlier work/play.log moves to work/logs/play-*.log (the five newest, and the three newest that ended in a crash, a hang or a lost GPU). After a session play.log has your home folder written as ~ and each run of one repeated line folded into one line with [repeated N times].
  • ChangedThe bug report form asks for the support package first, the version instead of a commit, and how you installed the port; it no longer asks you to edit your user name out of the log by hand.
  • ChangedA new look shared with the Killzone 2 and Killzone 3 ports (Project Pyrrhus and Project Helghast, by undecuple): the README banner, the social preview, the Windows setup's pictures and the program icons (now lettered KZ1) are drawn in steel blue with a V chevron by one script, tools/release/installer_art.py, with the Rajdhani font. The project page is now a game-style menu that shows one section at a time and works with the keyboard and a game pad, with a screenshot viewer, a light theme and a plain page without script.
  • ChangedThe setup, the launcher's page and the docs now say the first build takes 5 to 30 minutes instead of about five: on four cores and a hard disk it took close to half an hour (#134).
  • ChangedThe install and troubleshooting pages say that RPCS3 needs Microsoft's Visual C++ runtime on a fresh Windows, without which "Use my RPCS3 install" fails (#136).
  • ChangedThe first run takes the movies out of the game's archive faster and with less memory: each movie is written to its file as it is read, instead of being put together in memory first, which copied the whole movie so far at every block (tools/psarc_ls.py; on made-up data a 31 MB movie took 2.8 s of copying, now 0.01 s). An archive that is cut short is named in the error.
  • ChangedThe release folders no longer carry two sets of files that no build reads (glslang's test shaders and the registry Vulkan's headers are generated from): about 55 MB and 3,400 files less on disk after install, and about 5 MB less to download.
  • ChangedThe build no longer keeps a second and a third copy of FFmpeg's libraries and a second copy of the Vulkan headers: what it stages for the compile and beside the program are hard links to the toolchain folder's files where the file system makes them (NTFS, ext4, btrfs), and copies as before where it does not (exFAT). About 260 MB less disk on Windows and 280 MB less on Linux.
  • ChangedThe Linux folder is now a .tar.xz (project-vekta-X.Y.Z-linux.tar.xz), about a third smaller to download than the .tar.gz it replaces. tar xf unpacks it, and so do the launchers.
  • ChangedThe install and troubleshooting pages also say that on Windows 10 RPCS3's .7z needs 7-Zip to unpack, and that RPCS3 needs the graphics driver's vulkan-1.dll, which a Windows 10 without a driver lacks.
  • ChangedThe README is shorter and in the same shape as the Killzone 2 and Killzone 3 ports: a centred header, the status in key numbers and a table per platform, numbered install steps and the launcher badges. The detail moved to new pages: docs/STATUS.md, docs/PRIVACY.md (what goes online and where your data goes), docs/FAQ.md, docs/ACCESSIBILITY.md and docs/AI.md.
  • FixedThe setup's header image no longer touches the window's right edge (it sat flush at every display scale).
  • FixedA candidate fix for AMD Radeon RX 5000 and 6000 cards on Windows closing the game a few seconds into level 1 (#129), not yet confirmed on those cards: the GPU now reads zeros instead of undefined memory when a draw reads past the end of a buffer (Vulkan's robustBufferAccess, which NVIDIA's driver did not need). play.log says robustBufferAccess: on; PS3RECOMP_VK_ROBUST=0 turns it off for comparison (patch 2083).
  • FixedA second candidate fix for #129, from a tester's crash reports on an RX 6600: AMD's Windows driver closes the game while it compiles the MLAA pass (the game's anti-aliasing, redone as a GPU shader), every time, in the same place. On that driver the MLAA now uses a second form of its shader that does its arithmetic without 64-bit integers, the one thing it used that the glow and motion blur (which build there) do not: the picture is the same, byte for byte, and the RX 6600 that closed the game plays level 1 with it (patch 2087). Other cards keep the faster first form; cards without 64-bit integer support, which had no MLAA, now get it too. If a driver still closes the game while compiling it, the next start leaves the MLAA out on that driver (the glow and motion blur still run, the PC screen greys the Anti-aliasing row) and a new driver tries again. The log names each post pass as it compiles (building the MLAA pass, the MLAA pass: built in N ms); PS3RECOMP_MLAA_BUILD=1 builds it whatever happened before (patches 2086-2087). The log line GPU MLAA on local ...: ran now appears only when the MLAA itself ran; with it off or not built it says not applied and that the other post passes ran (patch 2088).
  • FixedThe build no longer stops at "Preparing the game's data" when the install folder's path has accented letters (a letter with an accent or a cedilla in a folder name): it said the game was not the tested version (#130).
  • FixedA PC without a working Vulkan driver now gets a message that says so when the game starts. Before, the game ran on with no window and closed after about 45 seconds without a word (#131).
  • FixedOn a CPU too old for the port, Project Vekta.exe says so at once. Before, the message could take 30 to 90 seconds on the first start after the PC was switched on, with nothing on screen meanwhile (#133).
  • FixedThe setup fits a 1280x800 screen at 150% display scale (Next and Cancel were under the taskbar), and its "Your game" page shows its three choices without a scroll bar at 125% and above (#135).
  • FixedAt 125% display scale the setup's "Your game" page shows all four choices and the note under them without a scroll bar or a cut line, and the DLSS page shows its whole text and checkbox.
  • FixedUninstalling removes the install folder again: a file the game writes at start (flashMP3.pic) and the empty folders the build left in work\vfs kept it there. Saves and settings stay, as before (#132).
  • FixedWhile the game loads, before its first frame, the window is now refreshed about 60 times a second instead of about 5,000, which kept a CPU core and the GPU busy for nothing.
  • FixedOn Linux, stopping the game (SIGTERM, Ctrl+C or the launcher) now works when the game is frozen: after 2 s it quits anyway, and a second Ctrl+C ends it at once. Before, only a forced kill did.

0.6.0

20 Nov 2026 · pre-release

  • Added"Get it on" badges for RecompLauncher and Quiver Launcher in the README, the install page and the project page, linking to the port's page on each. The RecompLauncher badge is the one from its press kit, unchanged; the Quiver badge is text only, since Quiver has no press kit and its logo is a mark. The project page's install box also lost its outdated lines: it lists the setup program and the release folders, and what goes online.
  • AddedKZ1HD.exe carries a version: Explorer's Details tab shows Project Vekta and the release, and KZ1HD --version (Windows and Linux) prints it with the patch set and the ps3recomp commit it was built from. The same line opens every log, so a log says which build wrote it.
  • AddedKZ1HD.exe has a Windows manifest: it declares Windows 10/11 and the per-monitor DPI awareness the game already asked for at run time.
  • AddedOne program to start in each release folder: Project Vekta.exe on Windows and the new project-vekta on Linux. With no arguments it plays, and before the first build it checks your files and builds first, asking nothing when RPCS3 and the game are in their usual places. It takes --game, --eboot, --psarc, --rpcs3 [DIR] (or KZ_GAME, KZ_EBOOT, KZ_PSARC), kept in work/paths.env, and --prepare, which checks and builds with no window or question and prints progress lines for a launcher. Each failure has its own exit code and fix text, one table for the game and the launcher (port/kz1hd/kz_exit.h, listed in docs/BUILDING.md). A missing Vulkan driver is named before the game starts.
  • Addedrecomplauncher.json at the top of the Windows and Linux folders, for launchers that read it (RecompLauncher): it names the game folder to ask for, the optional decrypted EBOOT.elf, the build step with its NVIDIA DLSS tick, the program to start, the saves, the logs and the exit codes. It is made from one source with the version stamped (tools/release/recomplauncher.py) and checked against a schema in the repository.
  • Addeddocs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md: what you see, what to do and what to attach, for each exit code; docs/INSTALL.md has a section on installing through a game launcher, and docs/dev/launchers.md the contract for launcher developers. CONTRIBUTORS.md lists who helped.
  • AddedA CPU that is too old is named instead of crashing. The game is built for x86-64-v3 (AVX2, FMA, BMI2: Intel Haswell or AMD Excavator and later). On an older CPU it used to stop at once with an illegal-instruction crash. Now the game says which level it needs and which one the CPU has (a message box on Windows, the launcher's message, the log), and exits with code 75. The first run's check and the Windows setup's first page ask the same before the build: the first run stops there, and the setup asks whether to install anyway.
  • AddedThe game checks that its EBOOT.elf is the one the build was made from (by size and SHA-256, in tens of milliseconds) before it starts. With another one (another version of the game, a file replaced after the build), it says so instead of running code that does not match, opens no window and exits with code 76; the launcher offers to rebuild. KZ_EBOOT_CHECK=0 skips it.
  • ChangedNo PS3 system software is needed any more. The music and the other MP3 streams are decoded by the port itself (minimp3, CC0) in place of the system software's MP3 decoder, which ran translated from your dev_flash; compared with it in Levels 1 and 4: the same frames, the same silences, samples within 50 dB SNR. The flashMP3.pic the game still asks for is a stand-in the port writes, with no code in it. The installers no longer ask for dev_flash or check its version; the RPCS3 route works with no firmware installed in RPCS3.
  • ChangedThe release folders keep their scripts in scripts/: run.cmd, play.cmd and the new prepare.cmd on Windows, run.sh, play.sh and prepare.sh on Linux, so that the launcher is the one program at the top (a launcher such as Quiver starts the one it finds there). An install over an earlier version removes the old run.cmd and play.cmd.
  • ChangedThe firmware's libsre.prx is no longer needed: the SPURS queue the game sends its compressed data requests through, which ran the firmware's own libsre code, is now in the port's runtime (ps3recomp patch 1022, checked against libsre on 46,000 random cases; after Project Pyrrhus patch 6003, MIT). The installers stop asking for it, and on the RPCS3 route your RPCS3 decrypts only the game's EBOOT. The lift no longer makes work/fw, and removes the one an earlier version made.
  • FixedThe Linux folder builds the game again: KZ1HD called mallinfo2, which the folder's own toolchain (glibc 2.31) does not have, so its link stopped with "undefined symbol: mallinfo2". Builds with the system's compilers were not affected.
  • FixedNVIDIA DLSS is offered on Windows only in the release folders: NVIDIA's Linux library is built for GCC's C++ library and does not link with the Linux folder's own toolchain, so a ticked DLSS stopped that build while compiling. The Linux folder now builds with AMD FSR 3.1 and says why; DLSS on Linux needs a build with the system's compilers (tools/install.sh).
  • FixedThe number of build jobs can be capped for any way the build starts: KZ_JOBS in the environment (a launcher started with it included) and --jobs N on the prepare step (scripts/prepare.sh, project-vekta --prepare), which before took only the memory-based default. For a PC that gets too hot or switches off while compiling (docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md).
  • FixedThe Linux folder's first build no longer needs about 18 GB of memory: its bundled compiler took that much on one file of glslang (the shader compiler the build includes) at the usual optimisation. glslang is now built optimised for size, and the whole step peaks under 500 MB.

Install

The setup program or the release folders: they check your own copy and build the port on your PC.

v0.7.0 pre-release

23 Nov 2026 · playable · Windows x64 and Linux x64

Download v0.7.0All releases

The release page has the Windows setup program (project-vekta-0.7.0-setup.exe, the easiest way on Windows), the Windows folder as a zip, the Linux folder and the source archive, each with a .sha256 file, and SHA256SUMS: check your download against them.

The Windows setup program, Project Vekta.exe in the Windows zip and ./project-vekta in the Linux folder check your own Killzone HD files (a disc or PlayStation Store copy, or the one your RPCS3 already installed), translate the game's code and build it on your machine. Nothing of the game is shipped or downloaded, and nothing is written into your game files. What each input must contain: Getting your files.

Through a launcher

The launchers install the Windows zip or the Linux folder and build the same way: installing through a launcher. They are third-party projects; their names are their owners' marks.

Or build from source

git clone --recurse-submodules \
  https://github.com/gustavomorinaga/project-vekta
cd project-vekta
tools/install.sh

Every step, and the Windows build: building.

What goes online

Nothing unless you choose it. The port, the setup and the build make no network connection of their own. The downloads are the ones you start (the release, or this repository and its ps3recomp submodule, the build tools) and two you opt into: NVIDIA DLSS, fetched from NVIDIA only if you accept its licence, and the new-version check, off by default. The whole list: What goes online; where saves and settings go: Where your data goes.

Viewing the main page loads the Rajdhani font from Google Fonts, which sees your visit; the repository, the setup and the game do not. The plain page loads no fonts.

Requirements

What you need from your own copy, and the PC it was tested on.

What you need

Your own Killzone HD (NPUA80856) from the Killzone Trilogy disc, installed, with its decrypted EBOOT (no PS3 system software is needed): GETTING-FILES.md. No PlayStation Network account is used.

About

Built on ps3recomp v0.19.0: PPU and SPU code lifted to C++, the RSX command stream replayed on Vulkan.

how it works · ps3recomp v0.19.0 · 164 patches

The port is built on ps3recomp (MIT), pinned at v0.19.0 with 164 patches of this project: the PPU code and the game's SPU programs are lifted to C++, the PS3 system libraries the game calls are reimplemented, and the game's RSX command stream is replayed on Vulkan. It builds natively on Linux, and on Linux for Windows; the Windows build is tested under Wine, Proton and on Windows.

It follows Project Helghast and Project Pyrrhus, the same method applied to Killzone 3 and Killzone 2, and reuses their general runtime work. About 65 % of Killzone HD is done, and 43 % of the whole trilogy plan; what comes next: the roadmap.
